newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian sunseed crop outlook varies -trade.
newsitem.headline: Russian sunseed crop outlook varies -trade.

text.p: Russia's 1997 sunflowerseed crop may better last year's disappointing outcome or even slip below it, depending on which analyst one speaks to, but domestic farms are eager to export to Europe, trade sources said on Monday.
"Russia will be very crucial to Europe this year," said a senior Western commodities analyst. "They (Europe) want the seeds."
Trade sources have various forecasts for sunseed output in Russia, a major producer and, with Ukraine, a swing supplier to Europe.
Nearly all agreed that about half the crop would be exported, although some seeds would be processed into vegetable oil in Europe and re-exported to Russia.

Most analysts said Russia's 1997 sunseed production would be flat or slightly above 1996's disappointing 2.75 million tonnes, which came as a shock after 1995's 4.2 million, Russia's best record ever.
Some analysts have pegged last year's output at as low as 2.1 million tonnes.
Andrei Sizov, head of independent agricultural consultancy SovEcon Ltd, saw the crop to be harvested this autumn at 2.7-2.8 million tonnes, with about 50 percent of it to be exported.
Sources said earlier hopes that output could push through to three million tonnes had been dashed by wet spring weather.
The United States Department of Agriculture forecasts output rebounding to 3.2 million tonnes from the previous year's 2.8 million.
But Arkady Zlochevsky, president of the OGO commodities house, said plantings had decreased and a wet summer could affect quality. He forecast output slipping to 2.5 million tonnes.
Exports could be flat on last year, Zlochevsky said, adding domestic demand would be high but buyers were unlikely to be in a strong position.

Russian and Ukrainian sunseed exports to the European Union last calendar year were 1.78 million tonnes, a 1.40 million tonne increase on 1995 levels, according to the independent Oil World newsletter.
Russia exported a quarter of its 1995 crop, more than double the previous year. The deliveries helped push prices down and kept some U.S. exports out of the European market.
Sizov put average harvests over 1991-1994 at 2.83 million tonnes, below official state figures of 3.1 million tonnes.

Sunseed plantings this year are down on the previous two years and below 1995/96's 4.12 million hectares, but are still Russia's third highest ever at around 3.5 million ha, according to state figures.

Russia has seen demand for oilseed meal fall against its shrinking livestock and poultry sectors. Domestic vegetable oil consumption, nearly always of sunseed oil, has been flat for years at a little over six kg per person, far below Western levels of 11-15 kg.
Sunflower, an attractive cash crop for Russian farmers, accounts for 85 percent of Russia's total oilseeds crop.
